football_evidence.question: Can Vanderbilt’s pass rush get to KJ Jackson?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 0.2 points.
supporting: When Arkansas has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Arkansas’ offense has allowed a sack on 6.9% of its dropbacks, and Vanderbilt’s defense sacks the quarterback on 7.2% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Arkansas has the ball (big plays on the ground): Arkansas’ offense turns 3.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and Vanderbilt’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.3% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
In his last two games (Texas A&M and Tennessee), Jackson averaged 5.1 yards per attempt, against 6.9 in his four games before that.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Vanderbilt’s offensive line No. 4 nationally and Arkansas’ No. 113.
contradicting: In his last two games (Auburn and Ole Miss), Curtis averaged 6.4 yards per attempt, against 8.4 in his three games before that.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Arkansas’ quarterback room No. 76 nationally and Vanderbilt’s No. 108.
quarterbacks: Jared Curtis has completed 82 of 131 passes (62.6%) for 968 yards, 7.4 yards per attempt, 5 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in five games for Vanderbilt, and has been sacked on 8 of 139 dropbacks.
Blaze Berlowitz has completed 27 of 52 passes (51.9%) for 375 yards, 7.2 yards per attempt, 1 touchdown and 1 interception in four games for Vanderbilt, and has been sacked on 1 of 53 dropbacks.
KJ Jackson has completed 110 of 186 passes (59.1%) for 1,193 yards, 6.4 yards per attempt, 7 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in six games for Arkansas, and has been sacked on 12 of 198 dropbacks.
AJ Hill has completed 16 of 28 passes (57.1%) for 181 yards, 6.5 yards per attempt, 1 touchdown and no interceptions in two games for Arkansas, and has been sacked on 4 of 32 dropbacks.

model: Vanderbilt’s defense has to come out ahead in the pass-rush matchup: it sacks the quarterback on 7.2% of opponent dropbacks, against an offense that has allowed a sack on 6.9% of its dropbacks.
Vanderbilt’s defense has to come out ahead on long runs: it gives up explosive gains on 8.3% of opponent runs, against an offense that turns 3.3% of its runs into explosive gains.
Vanderbilt’s quarterback situation has to settle: Jared Curtis has taken 52% of Vanderbilt’s recent dropbacks and Blaze Berlowitz 45%.
Home field has to be worth something close to the full 4.1 points EdgeDesk gives it.
